newsitem.title: ITALY: Cuba's Castro arrives in Rome for food summit.
newsitem.headline: Cuba's Castro arrives in Rome for food summit.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro arrived in Rome amid tight security on Saturday to attend the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit, witnesses said.

Castro, one of six vice-chairmen of the five-day summit which ends on Sunday, arrived on a special flight from Havana for a visit that may also include an historic audience with Pope John Paul at the Vatican .

A Reuters correspondent at Rome's Fiumicino airport said the 70-year-old communist leader, dressed in khaki uniform and surrounded by police, greeted a crowd of reporters but refused to answer any of the questions shouted at him.
Diplomatic sources said Castro was likely to deliver an address to the summit at the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) headquarters at around 1000 GMT.
The Cuban leader would later meet Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro. There were no details about any possible meeting with the Pontiff.

Castro is expected to use the summit stage as a golden opportunity to castigate Washington for a 34-year-old trade embargo against the Caribbean island and the recent Helms-Burton law designed to squeeze him out of power.
